beats: Hook: in RL for language models the slow part is not the training; it is waiting for the model to finish its answers. [line_rl_coach_waiting, line_rollout_long_tail]

One RLVR step: generate (GPUs) -> verify (CPUs) -> train (GPUs) -> sync the weights; generation is most of the step (speaker: about 70% at small scale, up to 90% at large; check). [line_gpu, line_servers, line_clock_face; library: L10-01's line_rl_checker_box]

The long tail: the batch starts full and compute-bound, then one or two long answers keep going while the GPU sits nearly idle (memory- and latency-bound) and training waits. [line_rollout_long_tail, line_gpu_cat_nap, line_receipt, line_long_ribbon]

Trick 1, low precision: generate in FP8 / FP4 (about 2x faster than BF16, check); the weights are re-quantized at every sync, and training must round the same way as generation (Jet-RL) or learning drifts. [line_rl_two_rulers, line_ruler_curve]

Trick 2, speculative decoding fits the slow tail, but the policy keeps moving: a frozen drafter goes stale and final accuracy drops below no drafter at all; keep training the drafter (ReSpec). [line_drafter_wrong_turn, line_drafter_trains_along, line_dog_chases_cat]
Trick 3, history rhymes: earlier answers to the same prompt form a suffix tree that drafts for free (RhymeRL). [line_past_answers_peek, line_rhyme_tag_tree]

Trick 4, async RL: start the next batch before the weight update; a rollout can mix weight versions (off-policy, bounded lag); about 2x generation throughput at lag 2 (rule of thumb, check); separate generation and training GPUs. [line_async_recipe_swap, line_gen_train_two_rooms, line_two_teams, line_d_servers]
Takeaway: generation is not compute-bound, so overlap batches instead of waiting for the slowest answer. [line_kitchen, line_d_chefs, line_gen_train_two_rooms]
Cover (line_cover_l10_02; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): an exam hall of robots: six finished and bored, two still writing scrolls that pour onto the floor.
